chapter_meta.description: Your opponent gives up the center to take your c4-pawn. You play for active pieces and the long diagonal, and you usually win the pawn back.

qc2.strategic_idea: You take control of the center.
qc2.explanation: You put your queen's pawn in the middle of the board: your first foothold in the center.
qc2.hint: Start by claiming the center with a pawn.

purpose.answer: You take control of the center with your queen's pawn.
wrong: You prepare to castle quickly on the kingside.
You start an early attack on your opponent's f7-pawn.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent stops you from playing e4.
qc2.explanation: Your opponent develops flexibly and controls e4, so you can't easily build a full pawn center with e2-e4.

qc2.strategic_idea: You attack d5 and open lines for your queenside pieces.
qc2.explanation: Your c-pawn fights for d5 and makes room for your queenside pieces.
qc2.hint: Use your c-pawn to fight for d5.

purpose.answer: You fight for d5 and make room for your queenside pieces.
wrong: You prepare to put your queen's bishop on b2.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent supports the center and frees the dark-squared bishop.
qc2.explanation: Your opponent prepares ...d5 and opens the f8-bishop's path to e7, d6 or b4.

qc2.strategic_idea: You prepare to fianchetto your king's bishop.
qc2.explanation: You make room on g2 for your light-squared bishop, which will aim down the long diagonal h1-a8.
qc2.hint: Prepare a home for your king's bishop on the long diagonal.

purpose.answer: You make room on g2 for your bishop, aiming down the long diagonal.
wrong: You stop your opponent's bishop from giving a check on b4.
You prepare h2-h4 and an attack on your opponent's king.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent sets up a solid anchor in the center.
qc2.explanation: Your opponent plants a pawn in the middle of the board and blocks your long diagonal for now.

qc2.strategic_idea: You put your bishop on its strongest square.
qc2.explanation: From g2 your bishop puts long-range pressure on your opponent's queenside.
qc2.hint: Develop your bishop onto the long diagonal.

purpose.answer: Your bishop puts long-range pressure on your opponent's queenside.
wrong: Your bishop stops your opponent from playing ...e5.
You prepare to trade your bishop for the f6-knight.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops and gets ready to castle.
qc2.explanation: Black keeps the d5-pawn for now. In this line it takes your c4-pawn two moves later, after both sides have castled.

qc2.strategic_idea: You control d4 and e5 and get ready to castle.
qc2.explanation: Your knight goes to its natural square, watches d4 and e5, and clears the way for castling.
qc2.hint: Develop your king's knight and get ready to castle.

purpose.answer: Your knight watches d4 and e5 and clears the way for castling.
wrong: Your knight protects your c4-pawn against ...dxc4.
Your knight heads for g5 to attack the h7-pawn.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent makes the king safe before the center opens.
qc2.explanation: Your opponent castles short quickly, before any fight in the center begins.

qc2.strategic_idea: You tuck your king away behind the fianchetto.
qc2.explanation: Your king is safe behind the g2-bishop and the pawns, and your h1-rook joins the game.

purpose.answer: Your king gets safe behind the g2-bishop, and your rook joins the game.
wrong: You prepare to push your f-pawn to f4 and attack.
Your rook comes to f1 to put pressure on the f7-pawn.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes your c4-pawn: the Open Catalan.
qc2.explanation: Black's d-pawn leaves the center to win a pawn. The long diagonal is no longer blocked on d5, and you can win the pawn back.

qc2.strategic_idea: You attack the c4-pawn at once.
qc2.explanation: Your queen threatens to take back on c4. From c2 it also watches the c-file and the diagonal to h7.
qc2.hint: Attack the c4-pawn with your queen along the c-file.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent prepares ...b5 to keep the pawn.
qc2.explanation: After ...b5 the c4-pawn would be protected, and Black would gain space on the queenside.

qc2.strategic_idea: You stop ...b5 from keeping the pawn.
qc2.explanation: Your a-pawn hits b5. If Black plays ...b5 anyway, you take on b5 and win the pawn back. Otherwise your queen takes back on c4.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent's bishop heads for c6.
qc2.explanation: From c6 it will face your g2-bishop on the long diagonal. On d7 it already eyes your a4-pawn, which your queen protects.

qc2.strategic_idea: You win your pawn back.
qc2.explanation: Material is level again, and your queen is active on c4. It still protects the a4-pawn.
qc2.hint: Take back the pawn on c4.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent's bishop takes the long diagonal.
qc2.explanation: On c6 it faces your g2-bishop and attacks your f3-knight and your a4-pawn.

qc2.strategic_idea: You develop your bishop and attack the f6-knight.
qc2.explanation: The f6-knight guards d5 and e4, two key squares on the long diagonal. Later you can exchange it.
qc2.hint: Develop your dark-squared bishop with pressure on the f6-knight.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent attacks your queen.
qc2.explanation: The bishop jumps to d5 with an attack on your queen. It also hits your f3-knight.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your queen steps back to c2.
qc2.explanation: On c2 it keeps protecting the a4-pawn and stays on the c-file, aiming at c7.
qc2.hint: Move your queen to a safe square where it still protects a4.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent chases your queen again.
qc2.explanation: From e4 the bishop attacks your queen and your f3-knight, and it blocks the diagonal from c2 to h7.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your queen goes back to c1.
qc2.explanation: There it is safe, stays on the c-file and protects your g5-bishop.
qc2.hint: Retreat your queen to a square where it protects your g5-bishop.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent attacks your g5-bishop.
qc2.explanation: The h-pawn asks the bishop to decide. You exchange it for the f6-knight.

qc2.strategic_idea: You exchange your bishop for the f6-knight.
qc2.explanation: That knight was an important guard of d5 and e4. Without it, your pieces have an easier time in the center.
qc2.hint: Exchange your g5-bishop for the knight that guards d5 and e4.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes back with the bishop.
qc2.explanation: Black keeps both bishops, and the f6-bishop now presses on your d4-pawn. Your f3-knight protects it.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your rook protects d4.
qc2.explanation: Your d4-pawn now has two defenders: the rook and the f3-knight.
qc2.hint: Bring your f1-rook to the d-file.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent stops your a-pawn and takes the b4-square.
qc2.explanation: Your a4-pawn can't move forward any more, and b4 becomes a home for a Black knight: the a5-pawn supports it there, and none of your pawns can attack it.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your knight develops and attacks the e4-bishop.
qc2.explanation: Black must decide: exchange on f3 or move the bishop away.
qc2.hint: Develop your b1-knight with an attack on the e4-bishop, without blocking the c-file for your queen.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent exchanges on f3.
qc2.explanation: Black trades the active bishop instead of retreating it. You take back with your bishop, and its long diagonal opens up to the b7-pawn.

qc2.strategic_idea: You take back with your bishop.
qc2.explanation: Your bishop hits the b7-pawn on the long diagonal. Your d4-pawn has no defender now, but taking it is a mistake.
qc2.hint: Take back on f3 with your light-squared bishop.

qc2.strategic_idea: Your opponent grabs your d4-pawn. A mistake!
qc2.explanation: The queen takes the pawn but lands on the d-file in front of your d1-rook. Only your d2-knight stands between them.

qc2.strategic_idea: You attack the queen and the f6-bishop at once.
qc2.explanation: Your knight moves away, so your rook now attacks the queen, and the knight hits the f6-bishop. After 17...Qe5 18.Nxf6+ gxf6 19.Bxb7 you get your pawn back, and Black's kingside pawns are broken.
qc2.hint: Move your d2-knight so that it attacks the f6-bishop and your rook attacks the queen.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent leaves the d4-pawn alone and plays solidly.
moves.explanation: The c6-pawn cuts your f3-bishop off from the b7-pawn and takes the d5-square.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight comes to c4.
moves.explanation: From c4 it attacks the a5-pawn and watches b6, d6 and e5. With the knight gone from d2, your rook protects d4 again.
moves.hint: Bring your d2-knight to a square where it attacks a5 and e5.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent keeps the bishop and retreats it to h7.
moves.explanation: Black avoids the exchange. On h7 the bishop is safe and still watches the diagonal toward b1.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight goes to b3.
moves.explanation: It protects d4, attacks the a5-pawn and can jump to c5.
moves.hint: Move your d2-knight where it protects d4 and attacks a5.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes control of b5 and d5.
moves.explanation: The c-pawn also clears c7 and b6 for Black's queen.

moves.strategic_idea: Your queen comes to c3.
moves.explanation: From c3 it protects d4 and your b3-knight, and together with the knight it attacks the a5-pawn.
moves.hint: Put your queen on the long dark diagonal, where it protects d4.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the knight and protects f6.
moves.explanation: From d7 it protects the f6-knight. If you exchange on f6, Black can take back with this knight.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop your knight to c3.
moves.explanation: It protects your a4-pawn and watches the b5, d5 and e4 squares.
moves.hint: Develop your b1-knight so that it protects your a4-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent attacks your g5-bishop.
moves.explanation: As in the main line, you answer by taking on f6.

moves.strategic_idea: You exchange your bishop for the f6-knight.
moves.explanation: Instead of retreating your bishop, you give it for the knight. Then you gain space on the queenside with b2-b4.
moves.hint: Exchange your g5-bishop for the f6-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes back with the knight.
moves.explanation: A knight is back on f6, where it guards d5 and e4 again, and Black keeps both bishops.

moves.strategic_idea: You gain space on the queenside.
moves.explanation: Your b-pawn controls a5 and c5 and prepares b4-b5 against the c6-bishop.
moves.hint: Push your b-pawn two squares to gain space on the queenside.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's bishop attacks your queen.
moves.explanation: The bishop jumps to d5 and hits your queen and your f3-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: You take the bishop at once.
moves.explanation: Taking is better than moving your queen again: after 14.Qd3? Black wins your b4-pawn with 14...Bxb4.
moves.hint: Take the bishop that attacks your queen with your knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes back with the e-pawn.
moves.explanation: The pawn on d5 attacks your queen, and Black has a pawn in the center again.

moves.strategic_idea: Your queen goes to b3.
moves.explanation: From b3 it protects your a4- and b4-pawns and attacks the d5-pawn.
moves.hint: Move your queen to a safe square where it protects both your a4- and b4-pawns.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent fixes your a4-pawn and takes the b4-square.
moves.explanation: As after 14...a5 in the main line, b4 becomes a home for a Black knight: the a5-pawn supports it there, and none of your pawns can attack it.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop your knight to c3.
moves.explanation: It protects your a4-pawn and watches the b5-square.
moves.hint: Develop your b1-knight so that it protects your a4-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight heads for b4.
moves.explanation: From a6 it can jump to b4, the square the a5-pawn has just secured.

moves.strategic_idea: You exchange your bishop for the f6-knight.
moves.explanation: Without the f6-knight, Black has less control of e4, and you can push your e-pawn there.
moves.hint: Exchange your g5-bishop for the knight that guards e4.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes back with the bishop.
moves.explanation: The f6-bishop now presses on your d4-pawn, which your f3-knight protects.

moves.strategic_idea: You build a pawn center.
moves.explanation: With pawns on d4 and e4 you control c5, d5, e5 and f5.
moves.hint: Push your e-pawn two squares to build a pawn center.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight lands on b4.
moves.explanation: No White pawn can chase it from there. It eyes the c2, d3 and d5 squares.

moves.strategic_idea: Your rook protects d4.
moves.explanation: It supports your d4-pawn from behind and gets ready for d4-d5 later.
moves.hint: Bring your f1-rook to the d-file.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent makes room for the bishop on b7.
moves.explanation: The b6-pawn also guards a5.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight heads for d3.
moves.explanation: From d3 it will attack the b4-knight, which none of your pawns can chase away.
moves.hint: Retreat your f3-knight on its way to d3.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the knight and attacks d4.
moves.explanation: Black doesn't protect the c4-pawn, so you can take it back at once. Your f3-knight protects d4, and after 9.Qxc4 your queen does too.

moves.strategic_idea: You win your pawn back.
moves.explanation: Material is level again. Your queen on c4 protects your a4- and d4-pawns.
moves.hint: Take back the pawn on c4.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent offers a queen trade.
moves.explanation: Black's queen attacks your queen, your f3-knight and your d4-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: You protect your queen and your f3-knight.
moves.explanation: If Black trades queens on c4, your knight takes back.
moves.hint: Develop your b1-knight so that it protects both your queen and your f3-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's rook joins the d-file.
moves.explanation: Behind its queen, the rook adds pressure on your d4-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: You protect d4 with a pawn.
moves.explanation: Now d4 has three defenders: the e3-pawn, the f3-knight and your queen. It faces the c6-knight and Black's queen, with the d8-rook behind it. Even 11.Qd3?, which still guards d4, would lose the pawn after 11...Nxd4.
moves.hint: Protect your d4-pawn with a pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent trades queens.
moves.explanation: The game becomes calmer without queens. You take back with your d2-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: You take back with your knight.
moves.explanation: Your knight is active on c4 and eyes b6, d6 and e5.
moves.hint: Take back the queen with your knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's bishop heads for c6 at once.
moves.explanation: Black doesn't protect the c4-pawn yet, so you can take it back right away.

moves.strategic_idea: You win your pawn back.
moves.explanation: Material is level again, and your queen is active on c4.
moves.hint: Take back the pawn on c4.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent protects the c4-pawn with ...b5 at once.
moves.explanation: Black skips ...a6, so nothing protects the b5-pawn yet, and your a-pawn can attack it at once.

moves.strategic_idea: You attack the b5-pawn.
moves.explanation: Your a-pawn hits b5, the pawn that protects c4.
moves.hint: Attack the b5-pawn with a pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes your a-pawn.
moves.explanation: Black is two pawns up, but both of them, on c4 and a4, are loose. And since the b-pawn left b7, only your own f3-knight stands between your g2-bishop and the a8-rook.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop your bishop and attack the f6-knight.
moves.explanation: The pawns on a4 and c4 are loose and can wait. First you put pressure on the f6-knight.
moves.hint: Develop your dark-squared bishop with pressure on the f6-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent attacks your g5-bishop.
moves.explanation: You answer by taking on f6.

moves.strategic_idea: You exchange your bishop for the f6-knight.
moves.explanation: That knight guarded d5 and e4, two squares on the long diagonal between your g2-bishop and the a8-rook.
moves.hint: Exchange your g5-bishop for the f6-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes back with the bishop.
moves.explanation: The f6-bishop now hits your d4-pawn and also watches g5.

moves.strategic_idea: You make two threats at once.
moves.explanation: Your knight leaves f3, so your g2-bishop attacks the a8-rook, which nothing protects. The knight also supports Qh7, which would be mate. Black must take the knight, and you take the rook.
moves.hint: Move your f3-knight so that it supports a mate threat on h7 and frees your bishop's diagonal.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes the knight.
moves.explanation: That stops the mate on h7, but the a8-rook is still hanging.

moves.strategic_idea: You take the rook.
moves.explanation: You have won a rook for a knight, and Black's two extra pawns make material level. Black's best is 12...Qxd4; then Nc3 and Nxa4 win back the a4-pawn.
moves.hint: Take the rook that your bishop attacks.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent pushes the b-pawn past your a-pawn.
moves.explanation: The b4-pawn takes the c3-square from your knight, but it no longer protects the c4-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight attacks c4 and frees your bishop.
moves.explanation: From d2 it hits the c4-pawn, and with f3 empty your g2-bishop attacks the a8-rook. Your d4-pawn loses its only defender, though.
moves.hint: Retreat your f3-knight so that it attacks c4 and frees your g2-bishop's diagonal.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent blocks the long diagonal.
moves.explanation: The c6-pawn shields the a8-rook from your g2-bishop. Black lets the c4-pawn go and will take your d4-pawn instead.

moves.strategic_idea: You win back the c4-pawn.
moves.explanation: Material is level for a moment, but your d4-pawn has no defender.
moves.hint: Take the c4-pawn with your knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes your d4-pawn.
moves.explanation: Black is a pawn up again, but the queen comes out early while Black's queenside pieces are still at home.

moves.strategic_idea: You chase the queen with your rook.
moves.explanation: Your rook takes the open d-file with an attack on the queen. You gain time for your development.
moves.hint: Attack the queen with your f1-rook.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's queen steps to c5.
moves.explanation: It attacks your c4-knight, which your queen protects, and eyes your f2-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop with an attack on the queen.
moves.explanation: Your bishop comes out and drives the queen away again.
moves.hint: Develop your dark-squared bishop with an attack on the queen.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's queen goes to the kingside.
moves.explanation: From h5 it eyes your e2- and h2-pawns.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop your last knight.
moves.explanation: It protects your c4-knight. Your e2-pawn looks loose now, but after 13...Qxe2? 14.Bf3 the queen is trapped: the most Black can get for it is your d1-rook.
moves.hint: Develop your b1-knight so that it protects your c4-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight attacks your e3-bishop.
moves.explanation: Together with the queen it also hits your h2-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight protects h2.
moves.explanation: From f3 it guards h2 and controls the d4- and e5-squares.
moves.hint: Bring your d2-knight to a square where it protects h2 and controls d4.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes your bishop.
moves.explanation: The knight on e3 attacks your rook, your queen, your g2-bishop and your c4-knight, so you take it at once.

moves.strategic_idea: You take back with the knight.
moves.explanation: Taking with your c4-knight keeps your pawns healthy: fxe3 would leave you with doubled e-pawns.
moves.hint: Take back on e3 with a knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent gives the b4-pawn a second guard.
moves.explanation: With pawns on a5 and b4, Black's queenside holds together, and the a8-rook can come out via a7.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight takes a central square.
moves.explanation: From d4 it attacks the c6-pawn, and your d1-rook protects it.
moves.hint: Put your f3-knight on a central square where it attacks c6 and your rook protects it.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the bishop to a6.
moves.explanation: It attacks your e2-pawn, which your queen and your d4-knight protect.

moves.strategic_idea: Your last piece joins the game.
moves.explanation: Your rook comes to the c-file behind your queen, and your pieces now aim at the c6-pawn.
moves.hint: Bring your a1-rook to the c-file.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent blocks the long diagonal with the knight.
moves.explanation: On d5 the knight shields the a8-rook and protects the b4-pawn, but the c4-pawn is still loose.

moves.strategic_idea: You win back the c4-pawn.
moves.explanation: Material is level again, and your knight on c4 eyes b6, d6 and e5.
moves.hint: Take the c4-pawn with your knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent attacks your d4-pawn.
moves.explanation: Black challenges your d4-pawn, which no piece protects.

moves.strategic_idea: You take the c5-pawn.
moves.explanation: You are a pawn up for the moment. Black can take back with the e7-bishop.
moves.hint: Take the pawn that attacks your d4-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's bishop attacks your c4-knight.
moves.explanation: Black develops with an attack on your knight instead of taking back on c5 at once.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight steps to e3 and hits d5.
moves.explanation: From e3 it attacks the d5-knight, the piece that blocks your g2-bishop.
moves.hint: Move your attacked knight to a square where it hits the d5-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight comes out and attacks c5.
moves.explanation: Black wants to win back the c5-pawn, which your queen protects.

moves.strategic_idea: You exchange knights on d5.
moves.explanation: Black has to take back with the e-pawn, and then your c5-pawn moves forward with an attack on the d7-knight.
moves.hint: Exchange your e3-knight for the d5-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes back with the e-pawn.
moves.explanation: Black's d5-pawn is now isolated, and it stands on your g2-bishop's diagonal.

moves.strategic_idea: You push the c-pawn and attack the d7-knight.
moves.explanation: Your c6-pawn is a passed pawn: no Black pawn can stop it on its way to c8. Taking the d5-pawn with 14.Bxd5 instead would only give an equal game.
moves.hint: Push your c-pawn and attack the d7-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's rook attacks the c6-pawn.
moves.explanation: Your queen protects the pawn, so it is safe for now.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop your bishop and support your c-pawn.
moves.explanation: From f4 it controls c7, the square in front of your c6-pawn.
moves.hint: Develop your dark-squared bishop to the square where it controls c7.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight comes to c5.
moves.explanation: It attacks your a4-pawn and cuts your queen off from the c6-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your rook attacks the d5-pawn.
moves.explanation: Now your rook and your g2-bishop both hit d5. If Black grabs your c6-pawn, 17.Bxd5 takes back a pawn and attacks the rook.
moves.hint: Bring your f1-rook to the d-file to attack the d5-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes your c4-pawn at once.
moves.explanation: Black grabs a pawn before developing the rest of the pieces. In this line you don't rush to win it back: you develop quickly and open lines instead.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop your knight and get ready to castle.
moves.explanation: Your knight protects d4 and clears the way for castling.
moves.hint: Develop your g1-knight toward the center, where it protects d4.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent prepares ...b5 to keep the c4-pawn.
moves.explanation: With ...b5 next, the c4-pawn would be protected.

moves.strategic_idea: You castle.
moves.explanation: Your king is safe, and your rook can come to the center later.
moves.hint: Bring your king to safety.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the knight and attacks d4.
moves.explanation: Your f3-knight protects the d4-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: You protect d4 with a pawn.
moves.explanation: Now the d4-pawn is safe, and your queen can come to e2, where it attacks c4.
moves.hint: Protect your d4-pawn with a pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the bishop to d7.
moves.explanation: It will keep the c6-knight protected once the b-pawn goes to b5.

moves.strategic_idea: Your queen attacks the c4-pawn.
moves.explanation: From e2 it hits c4. Black protects the pawn with ...b5.
moves.hint: Attack c4 with your queen from the square your e-pawn left.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent protects the c4-pawn with ...b5.
moves.explanation: The a6-pawn backs up b5, so the chain a6-b5-c4 holds for now.

moves.strategic_idea: You strike at the pawn chain with your b-pawn.
moves.explanation: After 9...cxb3 10.axb3 you stay a pawn down, but your a1-rook gets the half-open a-file, and your bishop gets the b2-square.
moves.hint: Attack the c4-pawn with your b-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes on b3.
moves.explanation: The b3-pawn attacks your a2-pawn. You take back with that pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: You take back with the a-pawn.
moves.explanation: You are a pawn down, but your a1-rook now attacks the a6-pawn down the half-open a-file.
moves.hint: Take back on b3 with a pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the bishop.
moves.explanation: Black gets ready to castle.

moves.strategic_idea: You develop your bishop on the long dark diagonal.
moves.explanation: On b2 it protects your d4-pawn, and the c1-square is free for a rook.
moves.hint: Develop your dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent castles.
moves.explanation: Black's king is now safe too.

moves.strategic_idea: Your rook takes the c-file.
moves.explanation: It attacks the c6-knight and puts pressure on the c7-pawn behind it.
moves.hint: Put a rook on the c-file, facing the c6-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight jumps to b4.
moves.explanation: It leaves your rook's line and eyes the c2- and d3-squares.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight jumps to e5.
moves.explanation: It attacks the d7-bishop, and with f3 free your g2-bishop now hits the a8-rook, which Black's queen protects.
moves.hint: Jump into the center with your f3-knight and attack the d7-bishop.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight comes to d5.
moves.explanation: It blocks your g2-bishop's diagonal and adds a defender to the c7-pawn, which your c1-rook attacks.

moves.strategic_idea: Your last knight develops to a3.
moves.explanation: It attacks the b5-pawn and can go on to c2 to challenge the b4-knight.
moves.hint: Develop your b1-knight to the edge, where it attacks b5 and can go on to c2.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's bishop steps back to e8.
moves.explanation: From e8 it escapes your knight and still protects the b5-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: You push the e-pawn and attack the d5-knight.
moves.explanation: Your pawns on d4 and e4 take the center and attack the d5-knight.
moves.hint: Push your e-pawn one square and attack the d5-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight retreats to b6.
moves.explanation: From b6 it eyes c4 and covers a8 in case the a-file opens.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight challenges the b4-knight.
moves.explanation: It attacks the b4-knight and protects your d4-pawn.
moves.hint: Bring your a3-knight to a square where it attacks the b4-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent protects the b4-knight with a pawn.
moves.explanation: The a5-pawn gives the knight a second defender.

moves.strategic_idea: You take the b4-knight.
moves.explanation: Black must take back with the bishop: 17...axb4? opens the a-file, and after 18.Rxa8 you win your pawn back with a much better game.
moves.hint: Take the b4-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight jumps to b4 before castling.
moves.explanation: It eyes the c2- and d3-squares, but Black's king is still in the center.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight jumps to e5.
moves.explanation: It attacks the d7-bishop, and with f3 free your g2-bishop now hits the a8-rook, which Black's queen protects.
moves.hint: Jump into the center with your f3-knight and attack the d7-bishop.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight retreats to d5.
moves.explanation: It blocks your g2-bishop's diagonal and attacks your e3-pawn, which your f2-pawn and queen protect.

moves.strategic_idea: Your last knight develops to a3.
moves.explanation: Together with your queen it attacks the b5-pawn, which the a6-pawn and the d7-bishop protect. Black still has to castle.
moves.hint: Develop your b1-knight to the edge, where it attacks b5.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent protects the c4-pawn with ...b5 at once.
moves.explanation: Black plays ...b5 before developing the queenside pieces. With the b-pawn gone from b7, only your f3-knight stands between your g2-bishop and the a8-rook, which nothing protects.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight jumps to e5 and opens the long diagonal.
moves.explanation: Now your g2-bishop attacks the a8-rook, so Black has to save it. Your knight also attacks the c4-pawn.
moves.hint: Jump into the center with your f3-knight and open your g2-bishop's diagonal.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent blocks the long diagonal with the knight.
moves.explanation: On d5 the knight shields the a8-rook. The e6-pawn and Black's queen protect it.

moves.strategic_idea: You attack the b5-pawn.
moves.explanation: Your a-pawn hits b5, the pawn that protects c4. If the a-file opens, your a1-rook will face the a8-rook, which nothing protects.
moves.hint: Attack the b5-pawn with a pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the bishop and protects the a8-rook.
moves.explanation: From b7 the bishop also protects the d5-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: You strike at the c4-pawn with your b-pawn.
moves.explanation: Your b3-pawn and your e5-knight both attack c4, and only the b5-pawn protects it. The b3-pawn also protects your a4-pawn.
moves.hint: Attack the c4-pawn with your b-pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent pushes the c-pawn forward.
moves.explanation: Instead of taking on b3, Black keeps a pawn deep in your half of the board. The d5-knight protects it, and your b1-knight attacks it.

moves.strategic_idea: You attack the d5-knight, the c3-pawn's only defender.
moves.explanation: If the knight moves away, nothing protects the c3-pawn, and your b1-knight can take it.
moves.hint: Attack the d5-knight with a pawn.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent protects the c3-pawn and gives up the knight.
moves.explanation: Now the b4-pawn protects the c3-pawn, a passed pawn only two squares from your first rank. After 11.exd5 Bxd5, Black has two pawns for the knight.

moves.strategic_idea: You take the knight.
moves.explanation: Black takes back on d5 with the bishop, and you have a knight for two pawns.
moves.hint: Take the knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes back with the bishop.
moves.explanation: The bishop attacks your g2-bishop and your b3-pawn, and it shields the a8-rook from your g2-bishop.

moves.strategic_idea: Your queen threatens mate on f7.
moves.explanation: Your queen and your e5-knight both attack f7, which only Black's king protects: Qxf7 would be mate. So Black has no time to take your b3-pawn, which your queen no longer protects.
moves.hint: Bring your queen to a safe square where, together with your e5-knight, it threatens mate on f7.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent attacks your queen.
moves.explanation: The g6-pawn also blocks your queen's path to f7, so the mate threat is gone. It is Black's only good move.

moves.strategic_idea: Your queen steps back to h3.
moves.explanation: From h3 it protects your g2-bishop. If Black exchanges on g2, you take back with the queen, which then attacks the a8-rook down the long diagonal.
moves.hint: Retreat your queen to a safe square where it protects your g2-bishop.

levels.title: 6...dxc4: your opponent takes on c4
levels.intro: You know this position from the Closed Catalan. This time your opponent doesn't support d5 with ...c6 but takes your c4-pawn. You win it back with your queen.
key_ideas: Your queen stays on the c-file while Black's bishop chases it: c4, c2, then c1.
Next you exchange on f6 after ...h6, then bring your rook to d1 and your b1-knight to d2.

levels.title: The exchange on f6 and the d4 trap

parts.intro: Now your opponent leaves the d4-pawn alone: 16...c6.
Your opponent can also keep the bishop with 15...Bh7.

levels.intro: Your opponent chases your g5-bishop with ...h6. You exchange it for the f6-knight, protect d4 and bring your b1-knight into play.
key_ideas: After 16.Bxf3 your d4-pawn has no defender, but 16...Qxd4? runs into 17.Ne4, which attacks the queen and the f6-bishop.
If your opponent leaves d4 alone, your d2-knight goes after the a5-pawn, with help from your queen after 15...Bh7.

levels.title: Two more 10th moves: 10...Nbd7 and 10...a5

parts.intro: First, 10...Nbd7: the knight comes out before ...h6.
Now 10...a5: the a-pawn takes the b4-square.

levels.intro: After 10.Bg5 your opponent doesn't have to chase your queen with 10...Bd5. Here are two other ways to play.
key_ideas: Against 10...Nbd7, gain space with b2-b4, take a bishop that comes to d5 with your knight, and protect a4 and b4 with your queen on b3.
Against 10...a5, build a pawn center with e2-e4, protect d4 with your rook and bring your f3-knight to d3 against the b4-knight.

levels.title: 8...Nc6 and 7...Bd7: the pawn comes back at once
levels.intro: Two ways your opponent lets you win the c4-pawn back at once.
key_ideas: Against both, take back on c4 straight away: Black doesn't protect the pawn.
After 9...Qd5, protect your queen with Nbd2 and your d4-pawn with e2-e3.

levels.title: 7...b5: a trick on the long diagonal
levels.intro: This time your opponent protects the c4-pawn with 7...b5 at once, without ...a6 first. You attack the b5-pawn and find a trick against the a8-rook.
key_ideas: Once the b-pawn has left b7, only your f3-knight stands between your g2-bishop and the a8-rook.
11.Ng5 threatens both Qh7 mate and Bxa8, so you win the exchange and material is level.
Then win back the a4-pawn with Nc3 and Nxa4.

levels.title: 8...b4 9.Nfd2 c6: a pawn for your development
levels.intro: Your opponent can also push past your a-pawn with 8...b4. You attack c4 with your knight and open your g2-bishop's diagonal.
key_ideas: Black wins your d4-pawn, but you gain time against the queen with Rd1 and Be3 and bring every piece into play.
Watch the e2-pawn: 13...Qxe2? loses the queen to 14.Bf3.
At the end your knight, queen and g2-bishop all aim at the c6-pawn.

levels.title: 8...b4 9.Nfd2 Nd5: your passed c-pawn
levels.intro: After 8...b4 9.Nfd2 your opponent can also block the long diagonal with the knight: 9...Nd5.
key_ideas: Your c6-pawn is a passed pawn, and your f4-bishop supports it.
Black's isolated d5-pawn is a target for your d1-rook and your g2-bishop.

levels.title: 4...dxc4 5.Nf3 a6: the b2-b3 break
levels.intro: Your opponent can take on c4 at once, on move 4. You develop quickly, then strike at Black's queenside pawns with b2-b3: you stay a pawn down, but you get open lines.
key_ideas: Against ...a6 and ...b5, break the pawn chain with b2-b3: you don't win the pawn back, you get open lines instead.
After 9...cxb3 10.axb3 you are a pawn down, but your a1-rook gets the half-open a-file and your bishop goes to b2.

levels.title: Black's knight goes to b4: your knights answer

parts.intro: Or the knight jumps first, before castling: 11...Nb4.

levels.intro: Black's c6-knight heads for b4. You jump into e5 with your knight and bring your last knight out to a3.
key_ideas: Ne5 attacks the d7-bishop and lets your g2-bishop hit the a8-rook.
After 11...O-O, e3-e4 attacks the d5-knight and Nc2 challenges the b4-knight.

After 17.Nxb4 Black must take back with the bishop, since 17...axb4? 18.Rxa8 wins your pawn back with a much better game. After 17...Bxb4 you are still a pawn down, but your active pieces make the game about level.

levels.title: 5...a6 6.O-O b5: a knight for two pawns
levels.intro: After 5...a6 6.O-O your opponent can also play 6...b5 at once. You open the long diagonal with Ne5, strike at Black's pawns with a4 and b3, and win a knight for two pawns.
key_ideas: Once Black's b-pawn has left b7, Ne5 lets your g2-bishop attack the a8-rook.
Against ...c3, e2-e4 attacks the knight that protects the pawn: Black gives up the knight for a second pawn.
On h3 your queen protects your g2-bishop. If the d5-bishop leaves the long diagonal, for example with 13...Bxb3?, your g2-bishop takes the a8-rook.
Watch Black's c3-pawn: the b4-pawn protects it, and it is only two squares from your first rank.
